claim: No-till agriculture sequesters soil organic carbon relative to conventional tillage.
method: Paired-plot field trials, no-till vs conventional. Soil cores taken to 30 cm depth (standard sampling horizon). Bulk density measured, SOC concentration measured by dry combustion, stock reported as Mg C per hectare. Effect = difference in stock between treatments. Meta-analyses pool these paired trials.
decision: agricultural carbon credit issuance and climate mitigation targets
native: soil organic carbon mass, Mg C/ha

claim: Microplastic particles accumulate in human tissue, with burden rising over recent decades.
method: Post-mortem and surgical tissue samples (liver, placenta, brain, carotid plaque). Tissue digested with KOH or enzymatic digestion to remove organic matter. Residue filtered. Particles counted and polymer-identified by pyrolysis-GC/MS or micro-FTIR. Burden reported as particles per gram or ug polymer per gram wet tissue. Archived samples of different vintage compared to assess trend.
decision: regulatory limits on food-contact plastics and packaging
native: particle count or polymer mass per gram tissue
source: WORK_ORDER.md section 3, transcribed; selftest checks the transcription against the order

claim: First-draw tap water in the sampled distribution system meets the lead action level.
method: One-litre first-draw samples collected at a fixed set of residential taps after at least six hours of stagnation. Lead measured by ICP-MS, reported as micrograms per litre per sample. The 90th percentile of the sample set is computed and compared to the action level of 15 micrograms per litre. The tap set is resampled each monitoring period.
decision: compliance determination of the sampled system against the lead action level
native: lead concentration, micrograms per litre, 90th percentile of first-draw samples
control_decision_quantity: lead concentration, micrograms per litre, 90th percentile of first-draw samples
